```{r}
#Converting the required columns to numeric 
ardd$Age<-as.numeric(ardd$Age)
ardd$Year<-as.numeric(ardd$Year)
ardd$Month<-as.numeric(ardd$Month)
ardd$`Speed Limit`<-as.numeric(ardd$`Speed Limit`)
```

```{r}
#trimming the spaces of text columns
ardd$State<-trimws(ardd$State)
ardd$Gender<-trimws(ardd$Gender)
ardd$Dayweek<-trimws(ardd$Dayweek)
ardd$`Road User`<-trimws(ardd$`Road User`)
ardd$`Crash Type` <- trimws(ardd$`Crash Type`)

```

### 5. Data conversion

```{r}
# creating Time vcategory categorical variable from time
ardd<-ardd%>%
  mutate(
   Time=trimws(Time),
   Hour=suppressWarnings(as.numeric(substr(Time,1,2))),
   Time_Category = case_when(
      Hour >=5 & Hour <12 ~ "Morning",
      Hour >=12 & Hour < 17 ~ "Afternoon",
      Hour >= 17 & Hour < 21 ~ "Evening",
      Hour >= 21 | Hour < 5  ~ "Night",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# creating seaon column using months
ardd <- ardd %>%
  mutate(
    Season = case_when(
      Month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Summer",
      Month %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Autumn",
      Month %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Winter",
      Month %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Spring",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
# cleaning the null values
clean_ardd<-ardd %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Time_Category),
    !is.na(Season),
    !is.na(Dayweek),
    !is.na(`Speed Limit`)
  )
clean_ardd$Dayweek<-factor(    # changing Dayweek to factor to maintain correct order
  clean_ardd$Dayweek,
  levels=c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday")
)
clean_ardd$Time_Category<-factor(   # changing Time_Category to factor to maintain correct order
  clean_ardd$Time_Category,
  levels=c("Morning", "Afternoon", "Evening", "Night")
)
clean_ardd$Season<-factor(      #Season toits factore to maintain order correctly in plots
  clean_ardd$Season,
  levels=c("Summer", "Autumn","Winter","Spring")
)
```

## Section-2

## 1. Line Graph

### Road fatalities in Australia from 1989-2025

```{r}
# Line graph for year-wise trend   
library(scales)                                                             # loading scales library
year_fatalities_trend <- clean_ardd %>%
  filter(!is.na(Year), Year<2026) %>%      # Filtering the data with year less than 2026
  count(Year)                                                               # counting the fatalities based on year


p1 <- ggplot(year_fatalities_trend,aes(x=Year, y=n,
                                       text=paste("Year:", Year,
                                                  "\nFatalities:", scales::comma(n))))+                             # plotting the graph
  geom_line(aes(group=1), color='#2c3e50',linewidth = 1.5)+                               # choosing line color
  geom_point(color='#e74c3c',size=2.3)+                                     # choosing the point color
  geom_vline(xintercept=2020, linetype="dashed", color="grey60")+           # plotting the line on break point to diffrentiate
    labs(
      title="Has Australia's three decade road safety ended?",
      x="Year",
      y="Number of fatalities",
      caption = "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026"
    )+
    scale_y_continuous(labels=comma)+                                    # Format y axis labels
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1990,2025, by=5))+                     # Arranging x-axis years from 1990 to 2025 by 5 years gap in between 
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13)+
    theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size=14),                   # Titile text is setting to bold, and size to 14   
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(color = "grey30", size=8),                 # subtitle text colour to grey
    plot.caption        = element_text(color="grey45",face = "italic", size=8), # Titile text is setting to bold
    panel.grid.major.y= element_blank()                                         # removing grid lines to make it clear
    )

p1_interactive  <- ggplotly(p1, tooltip='text') %>%
  layout(
    annotations=list(
      list(x=1989,                                                              # To highlight the starting point
           y=year_fatalities_trend$n[year_fatalities_trend$Year ==1989],
           text=scales::comma(year_fatalities_trend$n[year_fatalities_trend$Year==1989]),
           showarrow= FALSE,
           yshift=20,
           font=list(size=12,color="#2c3e50")),
      
      
      list(x=2020,
           y=year_fatalities_trend$n[year_fatalities_trend$Year ==2020],        # to hightlight the start point of reversal trending
           text=scales::comma(year_fatalities_trend$n[year_fatalities_trend$Year==2020]),
           showarrow= FALSE,
           yshift=20,
           font=list(size=12,color="#2c3e50")),
      
      
      list(x=2025,                                                            # To highlight ending year Ending
           y=year_fatalities_trend$n[year_fatalities_trend$Year ==2025],
           text=scales::comma(year_fatalities_trend$n[year_fatalities_trend$Year==2025]),
           showarrow= FALSE,
           yshift=20,
           font=list(size=12,color="#2c3e50"))
    ),
    shapes = list(

      list(type="line",
          x0 =2020, x1=2020,
          y0=0, y1=1,
          yref= "paper",
          line = list(color = "grey60", dash= "dash", width=1)) 
      ),
    xaxis = list(
      
      dtick=5,
      tick0=1990,
      rangeslider=list(visible =TRUE, thickness=0.1)
    )
      
    
  )
p1_interactive

  

```

## 2. Multi Line Graph

### Splitting the road fatalities by road user's

```{r}
# road fatalities trend split by road users
road_user_counts <- clean_ardd %>%
  filter(!is.na(`Road User`),
         Year >= 2010, Year <= 2025) %>%
  count(Year,`Road User`)
shared_road_user<- SharedData$new(road_user_counts, key = ~`Road User`)  #shared data creation with key as road user
p2  <- ggplot(shared_road_user, aes(x = Year, y = n, color =`Road User`, 
                                    group=`Road User`,
                                    text=paste("Road User:",`Road User`,
                                              "\nYear:", Year,
                                              "\nFatalities:", scales::comma(n))))+
  geom_line(linewidth = 1)+
  geom_point(size = 1.6)+
  
  labs(
    title    = "which road user's are affecting more in reversal trend",
    x        ='Year',
    y        ='Number of fatalities',
    caption  = "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026",
     )+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)+
  theme(
    plot.title          = element_text(face = "bold", size=14),    #Titile text is setting to bold

    plot.caption        = element_text(face = "italic", size=8),     #Titile text is setting to bold
    panel.grid.major.x  = element_blank())                         # removing grid lines to make it clear'
    
bscols(
  widths = c(3,9),
  filter_select("road user", "Select Road User:", shared_road_user, ~`Road User`, multiple =TRUE),
  ggplotly(p2, tooltip='text')
   
)


```

## 3. Horizontal Bar Graph

### Percentage increase in deaths by road user's from 1989 -2025

```{r}
# Incremnt of road user fatalities since 2020 in Australia
change_counts <- clean_ardd %>%                                              # Filtering the rows using year and road user                      
  filter(!is.na(`Road User`),
         Year %in% c(2020, 2025)) %>%
  count(Year, `Road User`) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Year, values_from = n, names_prefix ='y')%>%     # converts the data from long format to short 
  mutate(pte = (y2025/y2020-1)*100)                                         # calculate the percentage increment of road user fatalities from 2020 to2025
p3  <- ggplot(change_counts, aes(x = reorder(`Road User`,pte), y = pte, fill =`Road User`,
                                 text = paste("Road User:", `Road User`,
                                              "\n Deaths in 2020:", scales::comma(y2020),
                                              "\n Deaths in 2025:", scales::comma(y2025),
                                              "\n percentage change:",paste0("+", round(pte),"%"))))+ # ploting the bar graph and placing bars based on order
  geom_col(width = 0.8)+
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("+", round(pte),"%")), hjust= -0.1, fontface= "bold", size= 3.5)+  # creating the labels for percentage change
  coord_flip()+                                                                                # flipping the coordinates for better visual
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,55))+                                                         # setting the limits on y-axis
  
  labs(
    title              =  "How big is the change in vulnerable users?",
    subtitle           =  "Pedestrian and Motor cyclist fatalities nearly rose 40%",
    x                  =  'Road User',
    y                  =  'Percentage change (%)',
    caption            =  "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026",
     )+
  theme_minimal(base_size=13)+
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size=14),      #Titile text is setting to bold
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = "grey30", size=8),    # subtitle text colour to grey
    plot.caption       = element_text(color='grey50', face = "italic", size=8),     #Titile text is setting to bold
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),                           # removing grid lines to make it clear
    legend.position    = "none"
   
    )
ggplotly(p3, tooltip='text')

```

## 4. Lollipop Chart

### Distribution of Road Fatalities by states per 100,000 people

```{r}
# lollipop_chart- Road fatalities across different states in australia per 1,00,000 people
population_2024 <- tibble(                                                     # creating one table with staes and population using tibble()
  State = c("NSW","VIC","QLD", "WA", "SA","TAS", "ACT", "NT"),
  pop_states = c(8350000,6950000,5560000,2950000, 1880000,575000,475000, 255000)
)

state_fatalities <- clean_ardd%>%                                            # Filtering the data with year
  filter(!is.na(State), Year >= 2021, Year <= 2025)%>%
  count(State) %>%                                                           # counting the fatalities based on year
  left_join(population_2024, by="State") %>%                                 # joing population column to the repective states
   mutate(r = (n/5)/pop_states*100000)                                       # claculating the death per 1,00,000 people
p4  <- ggplot(state_fatalities, aes(x = reorder(State,r), y=r,
                                    text= paste("State:", State,
                                    "\nDeaths (5 years):", scales::comma(n),
                                    "\nDeaths per year:", round(n/5),
                                    "\nPopulation:", round(n/5),
                                    "\nDeaths per 100k people:", round(r,1))))+
                                                                              #ordering the bars based on highest - lowest
  geom_segment(aes(xend= State,yend=0),
               color='green', linewidth = 1)+                                 #plotting the lollipop chart using geom_segment and geom_point
  geom_point(color="red", size=5)+
  
  geom_text(                                                                  # adding the labels to the segments
  aes(label=round(r,1)),
    size=3.5,
    hjust=-0.3,
    fontface="bold"
  )+
  labs(
    title    = "How do states split the road fatalities in reversal trend?",
    subtitle = 'Remote and regional states have higher deaths per 100,000 people',
    x        ='State',
    y        ='Number of fatalities per 100,000 people  ',
    caption  = "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026",
 
     )+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)+
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size=14),         # Titile text is setting to bold
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(color = "grey30", size=8),       # subtitle text colour to grey
    plot.caption        = element_text(face = "bold", size=8),        # Titile text is setting to bold
    panel.grid.major.y= element_blank(),                              # removing grid lines to make it clear
    
    )
ggplotly(p4, tooltip="text")
  
  
  
```

## 5. Heat Map

### Distribution of Road fatalities by Days and Times across seasons

```{r}
#Heatmap plot using DayWeek,TimeCategory and season 
ardd_heatmap<-clean_ardd%>%
  filter(!is.na(Time_Category),       #Removing Null values using filter
         !is.na(Dayweek),
         !is.na(Season))%>%
  count(Dayweek, Time_Category,Season)
shared_season  <- SharedData$new(ardd_heatmap, key= ~Season)
p5  <- ggplot(shared_season, aes(x=Dayweek,
                       y=Time_Category,
                       fill=n,
                       text = paste("Day:", Dayweek,
                                    "\nTime:", Time_Category,
                                    "\nSeason:", Season,
                                    "\nFatalities:",n)))+
                       
      geom_tile(color="white")+                                                     # creates tiles in heatmap
      facet_wrap(~ Season) +                                                        # creates heatmap seperately for diffrent seasons
      scale_fill_gradient(                                                          # filling color density on fatalities frequency
        low="#fee5d9",
        high='#a50f15'
      )+
      labs(
        title = "Does temporal patterns changed over seasons?",
        subtitle = "The darkness of color represents represents frequency of road fatalities",
        x        ="Day of the Week",
        y        ="Time of the day",
        fill     ="No of fatalities",
        caption  = "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026",
        
    )+
      theme_minimal(
        base_size=13,
    )+
     theme(
       plot.title=element_text(face= "bold"),                  # Title text to bold to highlight the title
       plot.subtitle =element_text(color = 'grey35'),          # color of subtitle is changed to grey to differentiate,
       panel.grid=element_blank(),                             # Removing grid lines
       axis.text.x=element_text(angle=40,hjust=1)              # Angle of the x-axis text changed to 40, to avoid overlap
       )
     bscols(
       widths = c(3,9),
       filter_select("season_filter", "Select season:", shared_season,
                     ~Season, multiple = TRUE),
       ggplotly(p5, tooltip ="text")
     )
```

## 6. Stacked Bar Graph

### Road User Fatalities across Different Speed Zones

```{r}

# percentage of Road user fatalities across different speed zones
age_speed_data <- clean_ardd %>%                                                                    # Filtering the data using speed limit
  filter(!is.na(`Speed Limit`),!is.na(`Road User`),
         `Speed Limit`>=10, `Speed Limit`<=130) %>%
  mutate(speedzones=case_when(                                                                      # creating the speed zones
    `Speed Limit`<=50 ~"<=50 (urban)",
    `Speed Limit`<=60 ~"60 (suburb)",
    `Speed Limit`<=80 ~"70-80 (semi-rural)",
    `Speed Limit`<=110 ~"100-110 (rural)",
    TRUE               ~"110+ (Highway)"
  )) 
  
age_speed_data$speedzones <- factor(age_speed_data$speedzones,                                       # changing speed zones into categories using categories
                                    levels=c("<=50 (urban)", "60 (suburb)", "70-80 (semi-rural)", 
                                             "100-110 (rural)" , "110+ (Highway)"))
s_summary <-age_speed_data %>%
  count(speedzones, `Road User`) %>%
  group_by(speedzones) %>%
  mutate(pcte = round(n/sum(n)*100,1),
         total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()
p6 <- ggplot(s_summary, aes(x=speedzones, y=n, fill=`Road User`,
                                 text=paste("Speed Limit:", speedzones,
                                            "\nRoad User:", `Road User`,
                                            "\nProportion:", paste0(pcte, "%")))) +                                       # plotting the graph
  geom_col(position="fill", width=0.7)+                                                             # Filling different colors for different road users
  coord_flip()+
  scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +                                                       # formatting the y axis labels
  
  labs(
    title="which speed limits are dangerous for whom?",
    subtitle = 'Pedestrians are affecting more at low speed zones whereas drivers at high-speed zones',
    x='Speed Zones',
    y='pecntage of fatalities (%)',
    caption= "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026",
     ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +                                                 # setting the base_size=13
  theme(
    plot.title          = element_text(face = "bold", size=14),                   #Titile text is setting to bold
    plot.subtitle       = element_text(color = "grey30", size=8),                 # subtitle text colour to grey
    plot.caption        = element_text(color ="grey55" , face ="italic", size=8), #Titile text is setting to bold
    panel.grid.major.x  = element_blank(),                                        # removing grid lines to make it clear
    legend.position     = "bottom"
   
    )
ggplotly(p6, tooltip = 'text')
```

## 7. Stacked Bar Graph

### Single vs Multiple crashes at different times of the Day

```{r}
#Step 1-Removing Null values

clean_ardd_time <- clean_ardd %>%
  filter(!is.na(Time_Category),
         !is.na(`Crash Type`)
         ) %>%                          # remove NA value rows from time_Category
  count(Time_Category, `Crash Type`)    # counting no of rows on each category
# Step 2 — Plotting the graph
ggplot(clean_ardd_time,
       aes(x    = Time_Category, # ordering bars basedon count
           y    = n,                         # no of road fatalities
           fill = `Crash Type`)) +          # different color diffrent category

  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.8) + # using pre-counted n value, not using default count

  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(n)),   # presenting count on each bar
            position=position_stack(vjust=0.8),
            size = 3.2,
            color = "White",
            fontface="bold")+

  coord_flip() +                             # fliping the coordinates for better visualisation

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(          # Filling different colors for single and multiple
    "Single"   = "#e74c3c",
    "Multiple" = "#2c3e50"))+

  labs(
    title    = "Which crashes are dominant at what times?",
    x        = "Time Category",
    y        = "No of Road fatalities",
    fill     = "Crash Type",
    caption  = "Source: ARDD, Feb 2026") +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +  # setting base size of the text to 13
  theme(
    legend.position   = "bottom",   # crash type legend for single and multiple
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold"), #Titile text is setting to bold
    panel.grid.major.y= element_blank())      # removing grid lines to make it clear

ggsave("stacked_barchart_7.png", width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300) #saving the plot using ggsave
```

## 8. Box plot

### Road Fatalities analysis by Demographics

```{r}
#Removing the Null values if there are any in age and gender
ardd_age<-clean_ardd %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age),
         !is.na(Gender))
ggplot(ardd_age, aes(         #plotting the graph using ggplot
  x=Gender,                 #x-axis represents gender
  y=Age,                    #y-axis represents Age
  fill=Gender))+
  geom_boxplot(             #creates the box plot
    outlier.alpha = 0.10,   # setting size, alpha and width of the boxes makes faint, small, notch clearly visible respectively
    outlier.size=1,
    width=0.35)+
  
  stat_summary(
    fun=mean,            # calculates mean age for both categories separately
    geom="point",        # point in the both boxes represents means
    shape=18,            # shape is 18, it means diamond
    size=4,              #size to 7 to make it clearly visible
    color="black")+      # stting colour of the mean point to black
 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c(
   "Male"="#8e44ad",     # male-purple colour
   "Female"="#f1c40f"))+ #Female-Yellow color
  labs(
        title = "Which demographic groups are at more risk?",
        x        ="Gender",
        y        ="Age",
        caption  = "BITRE, Feb 2026",
        
    )+
   theme_minimal(base_size=12)+  #setting base size of the text to 12
   theme(
       plot.title=element_text(face= "bold"),             # title textto bold
       plot.subtitle =element_text(color='grey35',size=12),# subtitle text colour-grey 35 to distinguish with title
       plot.caption=element_text(color='grey30',size=8)  # caption color grey30
       )
     ggsave("Boxplot_8.png", width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300) # saving the plot as image using ggsave
  
```
